newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Palestinians lash Canberra over axed Arafat visit.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians lash Canberra over axed Arafat visit.

text.p: Palestinian authorities on Monday accused Australia of encouraging Israeli extremists and undermining the Middle East peace process by cancelling a planned visit by President Yasser Arafat.
Ali Kazak, head of the Palestinian Delegation to Australia, said the move highlighted Canberra's biased Middle East policy.
"It is undignified, contradictory, unprofessional and unfriendly to invite a leader and then have a change of mind," Kazak said in a statement.
"It reflects badly on the Australian government and further confirms Australia's biased and one-sided Middle East policy."
"It further damages Australia's international credibility, reputation and relations."
Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer told parliament on Monday the conservative Liberal-National government had decided not to go ahead with the planned Arafat visit.
"It is not convenient or suitable to process or progress that at this time," Fischer said without elaborating.
Kazak said the decision to cancel the visit contrasted with the government's close dealings with Jewish leaders.

"Unfortunately, this decision does not help the peace process. It gives encouragement and comfort to the extremist government of ... (Israel), which ... has brought the peace process to a dead-end and the situation to an explosive point."
Fischer, who is also trade minister, said Arafat was one of several Middle East leaders he had invited to Australia during a March tour of the region.
Other visits had also been cancelled because of inconvenient timing, he said.
Kazak said a visit by Arafat was long overdue.

"He has been invited by and visited nearly all countries around the world, such as Washington DC, London, Paris, Bonn, Stockholm, Tokyo, Pretoria, Jakarta, to name but a few, and also by Israeli President Ezer Weizmann," Kazak said.
